sophia-ml: Quick heads-up from a 12h int-stage soak on continuous-batching. We keep seeing short tenant microbursts (50-200 qps, ~2s) that arrive into a near-saturated batcher and trigger a ~2.5x P99 spike and ~800ms period of tiny batches. Posting observations + mitigations below.

aj-runtime: Drop the key metrics and likely root cause? :eyes:

sophia-ml: Metrics snapshot: baseline QPS ~12k, median batch size 18 tokens, median latency 22ms. During microburst windows batch size collapses to 1-3 for ~800ms; P95 stays ~stable but P99 jumps 110ms -> 280ms. KV cache hitrate drops ~7% concurrent with collapse.

kevin-sre: Any traces showing where the scheduler flips state? Is prefetch or eviction the stronger correlate?

sophia-ml: Short trace excerpt:
```
[trace] 00:01:34.122 enqueue tenant=T42 size=1 lane=microburst
[trace] 00:01:34.123 admit prefetch_budget=2 epoch=137
[trace] 00:01:34.124 schedule drain window=16ms
[trace] 00:01:34.896 kvcache miss tenant=T13 key=ctx_... -> eviction T13
[trace] 00:01:34.900 batch emit size=2 latency=240ms
```
Correlation looks like: early microburst join -> scheduler flips to eager drain / preempt -> prevents coalescing for other lanes -> KV misses rise -> p99 spike.

lia-eng: Patch or refactor?

sophia-ml: Phased approach: short-term conservative tweak + medium-term interface refactor.

1) Short-term (config + canary): Add per-tenant "prefetch_budget" and an "epoch_drain_grace_ms". Default keeps old behavior. If prefetch_budget>0 new joins use SOFT_PREFETCH: they reserve a tiny headroom slot but do NOT flip global drain state; then wait up to epoch_drain_grace_ms to coalesce. Minimal code path change and reversible via feature-flag.

2) Medium-term (scheduler interface refactor): Split Batcher->Scheduler surface into RequestJoin/CommitOrAbort semantics so join intent carries a mode hint: LATE_JOIN, SOFT_PREFETCH, IMMEDIATE_DRAIN. Scheduler returns an opaque JoinToken which owns any reservation; caller later commits or aborts. This eliminates internal hard-preemption inside scheduler and makes token lifecycle explicit.

Proto sketch for discussion:
```
enum JoinMode { LATE_JOIN = 0; SOFT_PREFETCH = 1; IMMEDIATE_DRAIN = 2; }
message JoinRequest { string tenant = 1; int32 size_hint = 2; JoinMode mode = 3; }
message JoinResponse { string token = 1; int32 slot_alloc = 2; }
```

aj-runtime: For canary default prefetch_budget=1 and epoch_drain_grace_ms=12ms, run 10% pods -> 50% if stable. Need telemetry: per-tenant coalesce wait hist + join_mode label.

kevin-sre: Watch memory/KV working-set amplification: soft-prefetch holds tiny refs longer. Propose a global prefetch reservoir and per-tenant cap; also add evict_hint(tenant, token) API so eviction thread can soft-evict pinned entries.

lia-eng: Token semantics: scheduler must own token lifecycle and be opaque. Tests for token expiry/retry and idempotency needed.

sophia-ml: Agreed. Plan to add token expiry auto-abort path (token TTL) so stale reservations free automatically.

coordinator-bot: deploy-note: feature-flag "soft_prefetch_v1" created on int-stage, rollout=10% pods. :robot_face:

aj-runtime: Action items:
- sophia-ml: RFC follow-up with proto sketch + telemetry table (owner)
- lia-eng: unit tests for token lifecycle/expiry (owner)
- kevin-sre: sim mem/kv patterns and propose reservoir limits (owner)
- aj-runtime: canary config + dashboards (owner)

sophia-ml: I'll post RFC diff today. Running a 6h canary at 10% then 50% if no regressions. Thanks all :thumbsup:

kevin-sre: One more: check eviction thread interactions; prefetched reservations should be hinted, not block eviction. I'll sketch an evict_hint API.

lia-eng: ack. I'll add token harness to batcher unit tests.

sophia-ml: Filing RFC follow-up link when ready. Closing thread for now.
